title: Level 3 (Advanced) - A-19
notes:
West leads the ♠Q against 3NT. South should win the opening spade lead as a club shift would not be welcome. South must try to take 5 diamond tricks. 2 spade tricks, the ♥A, and ♣A will account for the rest of South's 9 tricks.

South has only one play to guarantee 9 tricks regardless of how diamonds lie. South should cross to the ♥A at trick 2 and lead a low diamond from the dummy. If diamonds are 2-2 or 3-1, the ♦A and ♦K will take care of all of the defenders' diamonds after the first round has been ducked.

If East has all 4 diamonds and takes the ♦Q, he sets up South's ♦J. The diamonds are not blocked and South will take 5 tricks in that suit. If East ducks, South wins the ♦J and ducks a diamond to East. Again South will score 5 diamond tricks.

If West has all 4 diamonds East will show out on the first round of diamonds. South plays the ♦J (a low diamond would also work). If West ducks, South will take 6 diamond tricks. West thus wins the ♦Q, but South can take 5 diamond tricks by taking the marked finesse against West's ♦10.
